tagline.text: An open-air amusement park behind SM City Pampanga, home to the 65 m Pampanga Eye Ferris wheel

children.text: An open-air SM amusement park behind SM City Pampanga in San Fernando, Pampanga. It opened in November 2014 and has more than 20 rides, including the roughly 65 m Pampanga Eye Ferris wheel, a loop roller coaster and a drop tower.

Sky Ranch Pampanga is an open-air amusement park attached to the back of the SM City Pampanga shopping mall in San Fernando, Pampanga. Its name makes many people assume it is in Angeles or Clark, but it is actually off Jose Abad Santos Avenue in San Fernando, a different area from the Clark Freeport. From Manila it is about 65–80 km north along NLEX, and English Wikipedia says the park opened on November 30, 2014.

Sky Ranch is an amusement park brand that SM Prime Holdings runs at several locations. The Tagaytay branch is the best known, while the Pampanga branch sits right behind the mall, which makes it easy to combine with shopping and meals. The park spreads across an open-air area at the back of the mall, and its centerpiece is the Pampanga Eye Ferris wheel, about
tall. It also has a loop roller coaster that spins 360 degrees, a drop tower, a Super Viking, and many gentle rides for children such as a carousel, tea cups and a train.

Entry is normally free, and you pay per ride. If you plan to ride several attractions, it is much cheaper to buy a ride-all-you-can pass in advance from sites such as Klook or SM Tickets. A good plan is to stop by for a Ferris wheel ride and a few other rides, then spend the rest of the time eating and shopping at SM City Pampanga, which fills the day nicely. If you expect the scale of the roller coaster or drop tower to be huge, it is a little modest, but it is an easy stop for families with children and for travelers who want to spend a few hours on the way through.

Hours and prices change often and differ slightly by source. The figures here were cross-checked against a 2022 local blog, a July 2026 guide, Wikipedia and the SM mall directory, so please check the latest announcements on the official Sky Ranch social media pages or a booking site before you go.

, and on a clear day you can look out over the Pampanga plain. The most popular slot is around sunset, between

The most thrilling ride in the park, with a 360-degree loop. Riders must be at least
122 cm
(4 ft) tall, and pregnant women and people with heart conditions cannot ride. Rather than expecting a big theme park coaster, think of it as a short, intense ride.

The drop tower rises about 40 feet and then free-falls, and the Super Viking is a pirate-ship style ride with open seats that swing up to 90 degrees. The drop tower's height minimum is 4 ft, consistent across 2015 and 2021 announcements, and the Super Viking is reported to be similar, so check the height sign at the ride. With a 4 ft minimum, children in the lower elementary grades and younger cannot ride. Closed-toe shoes such as sneakers are reportedly required for thrill rides, so avoid sandals.
The Field Runner is a family roller coaster for riders at least
106 cm

(3.5 ft) tall, and children under 4 ft must ride with an adult, according to a recent guide; older guides list no limit, so check the height sign at the ride. The Sky Cycle is a pedal ride along an elevated track about
5 m
high and
long, which is not scary and has good views, so it suits parents and children together.

There are many gentle rides, including Wonder Flight, the double-deck carousel, Canoe River, Convoy Tour, pedal boats, the Safari Train, Pop-Ups and Cartoon Mill. A local blog singles out Wonder Flight as a ride to recommend for kids. Most have low or no height limits, which makes them convenient for families with young children.

blocks.title: Bumper cars, bumper boats and game booths

children.text: The bumper cars and bumper boats are rides where families and friends bump into each other for fun. There are also game booths such as basketball, ring toss and darts where you can win prizes. Games cost extra, so set a budget in advance.

The park is right behind the mall, so when it rains or gets hot you can go inside to rest and eat. If you use the mall annex exit, you can walk straight in, and when it rains the outdoor rides stop and resume about
20–30 minutes
after the rain ends.
On weekdays the park usually opens at noon. Arrive, check your all-ride pass and get your wristband. For an online voucher, just show the screen.
While the lines are short, take the family rides with low height limits first, such as the carousel, Wonder Flight and the Safari Train.
Ride the Sky Cycle, Field Runner and bumper cars. The midday sun is strong, so use a hat or a portable fan.
Go into SM City Pampanga for snacks and a rest. If it rains, move this break earlier.
Ride the Pampanga Eye around sunset. An all-ride pass usually includes one ride.
Measuring your children's height in advance reduces disappointment at the ride entrance. Height limits follow the height signs posted at each ride queue and are strictly enforced.

items.title: Thrill-focused 2–3 hour plan
items.subtitle: Loop roller coaster and drop tower

children.text: Weekday afternoons are relatively quiet. Start with the loop roller coaster.
Ride the drop tower and the Super Viking back to back. Be sure to wear closed-toe shoes.
Try the game booths for prizes or have a snack.
Watch the sunset from the Pampanga Eye, have dinner in the mall and head back to your lodging.
One guide says hours extend late into the night from Friday to Sunday and on holidays, but this is hard to confirm officially. Check the official social media pages before your visit.

From Manila-area terminals such as Caloocan, Cubao and PITX, take a northbound Victory Liner or Genesis Transport bus on a route toward Olongapo, Balanga or Mariveles, and get off at SM Pampanga or Robinsons Starmills. The fare is about
, and the trip takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–3 hours
depending on traffic.

After getting off, walk toward the mall annex and enter the park. Tell the bus conductor in advance that you are getting off at SM Pampanga. Buses marked for Dau or Mabalacat may not stop in San Fernando.
One guide says it takes about an hour from Manila in good traffic, but NLEX gets congested on weekends and long holidays.
Take NLEX and exit at Mexico, then drive south for about
5–10 minutes
. This is close, while the San Fernando exit is said to be heavily congested.
The open-air lot at the SM City Pampanga annex is reported to be free, and slow EV charging is also reported to be free. The motorcycle parking area is a little farther away.
From Clark International Airport or Angeles, take Grab or a taxi, or a jeepney or bus, into San Fernando. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so check on the spot.
From downtown San Fernando, you can take a jeepney to SM City Pampanga.
Sky Ranch Pampanga is an outdoor park and is strongly affected by the weather. Outdoor rides stop when it rains, so going in the dry season is the safer choice.

In terms of crowds, Tuesday to Thursday afternoons are the quietest, while weekends and Christmas holidays from November to January are very crowded. In December, the Giant Lantern Festival period in San Fernando overlaps and brings even more people.

Inside the park there are small kiosks selling hot dogs, popcorn, cotton candy and cold drinks. Security at the entrance does not allow outside food and drinks, but personal water bottles and infant formula are reportedly permitted. For a proper meal, it is easier and gives more choice to eat at the food court and restaurants of SM City Pampanga right next door.

Most people find lodging in downtown San Fernando or around Angeles and Clark. A day trip from Manila is possible, but if you also want to enjoy Pampanga's food culture, it is better to stay a night or two and combine downtown San Fernando with the Bacolor area.
It is much cheaper to buy the all-ride pass in advance on sites such as Klook, SM Tickets or MetroDeal than at the gate. Digital vouchers are reported to be valid for 180 days from purchase.
Senior and PWD discounts are about 20% when you show an ID at a walk-in purchase, but reportedly cannot be combined with online discounts.
Closed-toe shoes are reportedly required for thrill rides. You may not be allowed to ride in slippers or sandals, so wear sneakers.
When a shower hits, outdoor rides stop, so keep your wristband, wait inside the mall and ride again afterward.
One guide says there are no official paid lockers, so carry only the minimum.
The Pampanga Eye is popular around sunset,
to
, and lines get long. If you want to see the sunset, line up early.
The park is flat and paved, so strollers can generally get around.
Prepare your ID and your digital voucher screen so they open even when you are offline.
Pregnant women, people with heart conditions, recent surgery, back problems or severe motion sickness cannot ride the loop roller coaster, drop tower or Super Viking. Height limits are strict.
Hours differ by source, with one guide listing noon to 21:00 on weekdays and another listing 10:00 to 23:00 from Friday to Sunday and on holidays. Check the latest announcement before you go.
An entry fee may apply in peak season, and all-ride pass prices change often.
Outdoor rides do not run on rainy days, so consider changing your schedule before you consider an umbrella.
Buses marked for Dau or Mabalacat may not stop in San Fernando, so be sure to confirm with the conductor.
Prices and facilities differ from those at other Sky Ranch parks run by SM Prime, such as the Tagaytay branch.
The provincial capital of Pampanga, famous for its Christmas lantern festival. It is in the same city as the park, so it fits easily into your plan.
The site of a church buried by lahar from the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption. It is close to San Fernando.
The Angeles and Clark Freeport Zone area has many airport links, hotels and restaurants. It is a good base for lodging and getting around.
An isolated volcano rising from the middle of the Pampanga plain and a popular trekking destination.
